qt: to the Commission Carles Puigdemont i Casamajó (NI), Antoni Comín i Oliveres (NI) Subject:

The Mediterranean Corridor (MC) is the main east-west axis in the TEN-T Network south of the Alps. It will provide a multimodal link for the ports of the western Mediterranean with the centre of the EU. Multimodal connections with ports in Spain have yet to be developed1. The TEN-T network is therefore a strategic network to guarantee and enhance the mobility of both people and goods. Last December the Spanish ministry of transport awarded a contract for the comprehensive remodelling of the Madrid-Vicálvaro terminal, a project to which it will allocate more than EUR 300 million2, financed with Next GenerationEU funds. This prioritising of funding is detrimental to the Mediterranean Corridor. Six key milestones of the MC that were pending in 2022 are still pending3, meaning that construction deadlines for the MC are not going to be met. 1.
Is the Commission aware of the delays in the construction of the MC?
How is the Commission ensuring that Spain and other Member States use EU funds for priority projects such as the MC?
How does the Commission ensure that the MC is meeting all agreed deadlines and milestones?

(17 April 2024) Regulation 1315/2013 on Union guidelines for the development of the trans-European transport network (TEN-T) (4) provides for a long-term strategy with the identification of investment priorities for the completion of the core and comprehensive networks. Member States are expected to complete the core sections of the TEN-T network by 2030, in line with the standards set out in the TEN-T Regulation. In order to support Member States on their investment plans the Commission co-finances the development of the TEN-T network by means of the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) (5). Since 2014, the Commission co-financed 173 projects in Spain, with the EU contribution of EUR 1,299 billion (6). With regard to the Mediterranean Corridor, between 2018 and 2023, Spain tendered contracts worth EUR 4,9 billion and constructed for the total value of EUR 2,2 billion. The overall investment goal is the further expansion of the European standard track gauge along the Mediterranean coastline with the ongoing works between Barcelona-Tarragona-Valencia-Murcia-Almeria, investments in logistics nodes (upgrades of Can Tunis and La Llagosta RRTs, for example), and constructions within urban nodes, including ports. The European Coordinator for the Mediterranean Core Network Corridor monitor progress of works in the Corridor’s Work Plan (7). Transport sections that require further attention and acceleration in terms of planning are highlighted in the document. The Commission considers that substantial efforts are made by Spain to realise the TEN-T network.
